verdicts.reproduction: Reproduced with my OWN independent implementations (review/work/47/verify/, vectorized energy functions, not the first pass's files). Official joint mode (steptest --problem 47 --step 47.4): gold PASS; my bit-protocol mirror (full_mirror.py) PASS; three spec-compliant Metropolis variants all FAIL with AssertionError on np.allclose(E_trace, target): (a) full_alwaysuniform.py — IDENTICAL protocol except the acceptance is written as the mathematically equivalent 'np.random.random() < np.exp(-beta*dU)' which also draws the uniform on downhill moves: FAILS test 1 even seeded (verified with --isolate --test 1: FAIL); (b) full_single.py — one single-particle trial per MC step (the literal reading of the background's scheme): FAIL; (c) full_ordered.py — sweep displacing atoms in order instead of np.random.randint selection (a standard sweep idiom): FAIL. The frozen (1001,)-length trace for test 1 (64 atoms x 1000 sweeps = 64,000 trials; note the test's 'N = 32' comment is misleading — initialize_fcc(32) builds 4^3 = 64 atoms; the first pass's '32 atoms' phrasing was wrong on this detail but it does not affect the verdict) is reproducible ONLY by matching gold's exact draw sequence: randint selection, sqrt(dispSize)*normal(size=3), and uniform-skipping short-circuit acceptance — none of which the prompt, docstring, or background states, and one of which (Gaussian kernel) the background actively contradicts. Severity blocker stands: spec-compliance does not determine a pass; only the single unstated gold protocol passes.

fix.before: Write a function to use Markov Chain Monte Carlo simulation to generate samples energy of system of atoms interacting through Lennard Jones potential at temperature T, using Metropolis-Hasting Algorithm with Gaussian trial move.
fix.after: Write a function to use Markov Chain Monte Carlo simulation to generate samples energy of system of atoms interacting through Lennard Jones potential at temperature T, using Metropolis-Hasting Algorithm with Gaussian trial move. Use exactly this protocol so results are reproducible under a fixed numpy random seed: each MC step consists of exactly N single-particle trials (N = number of atoms). Per trial, in this order: (1) select the atom with tag = np.random.randint(0, N); (2) propose r_new = positions[tag] + np.sqrt(dispSize) * np.random.normal(size=3); (3) compute dU = U_i(r_new, tag, positions, sigma, epsilon) - U_i(positions[tag], tag, positions, sigma, epsilon); if dU <= 0 accept immediately WITHOUT drawing a uniform, otherwise accept iff np.random.random() < np.exp(-dU/T). On acceptance overwrite positions[tag] with r_new and add dU to the running total energy. Append the running total energy to E_trace once at the end of each MC step; E_trace starts with U_system(init_positions, sigma, epsilon), so its length is MC_steps+1.
fix.side_effects: Preserves all frozen h5 targets (test 1 stays valid). Turns the step into protocol transcription rather than algorithm design — acceptable trade-off; the alternative (replace exact-trace asserts with statistical-property checks on the equilibrated tail) is scientifically nicer but requires redesigning all three tests and regenerating all targets. The docstring dispSize line and the background's uniform-move text must be updated consistently (see the D4/D10 fixes below), and the same sentence should be added to problem_description_main.

Docstring says only 'dispSize: Size of displacement in Gaussian trial move, float'; gold uses np.sqrt(dispSize)*normal (variance reading). My std-dev variant (full_std.py, dispSize*normal, otherwise bit-identical protocol): '--isolate --test 1' PASSES (dispSize=1.0 makes sqrt a no-op, identical RNG stream), joint mode FAILS at the SECOND assert (traceback line 94 vs line 77 for first-assert failures), i.e. exactly at test 2 where dispSize=2.0 — precisely as the first pass claimed. 'Size of displacement' more naturally reads as std-dev (or maximum displacement, per the background); the passing reading is the counterintuitive one.

verdicts.reproduction: Static: sub_steps[3].step_background says 'Give this particle a random displacement, r(o) -> r(0)+\Delta(Ranf-0.5), where \Delta/2 is the maximum displacement' — a UNIFORM proposal (Frenkel-Smit style) — while the prompt and header demand a 'Gaussian trial move'. Direct contradiction on exactly the kernel the frozen trace makes load-bearing. Minor is right for scoring (header pins Gaussian) but the background misleads on the D5-critical detail.

fix.before:
Give this particle a random displacement,
$$
\mathbf{r}(\mathbf{o}) \rightarrow \mathbf{r}(\mathbf{0})+\Delta(\operatorname{Ranf}-0.5),
$$
where $\Delta / 2$ is the maximum displacement. The value of $\Delta$ should be chosen such that the sampling scheme is optimal.
fix.after:
Give this particle a random Gaussian displacement,
$$
\mathbf{r}(o) \rightarrow \mathbf{r}(o) + \sqrt{\mathrm{dispSize}}\,\boldsymbol{\eta}, \quad \boldsymbol{\eta} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, I_3),
$$
where dispSize is the per-coordinate variance of the trial displacement.
fix.side_effects: None; aligns background with prompt, header, and gold.

summary: All 7 first-pass findings CONFIRMED at their original severities (0 refuted, 0 uncertain); every dynamic claim reproduced with my own independent implementations, including the decisive ones (gold passes joint but fails tests 2-3 isolated; a mathematically equivalent acceptance rule fails test 1 even seeded; the std-dev reading of dispSize passes test 1 and fails exactly at test 2). Steps 47.1-47.3 are clean and fair as-is. The problem is fixable to fair with moderate effort: the cheap route is a protocol-prescribing prompt_edit for 47.4 (preserves all frozen targets) plus seeds-and-regen for tests 2-3 and three small doc edits; the nicer-but-costlier route replaces exact-trace matching with statistical-property tests.
